=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-side review of the Seller's SPA package

**Preliminary point on the "Reviewer Efficiency Note".** I have not accepted the [STANDARD] labels or the statement that the disclosure framework and limitation package are "already accepted". That is the Seller's own assertion, and nothing on our side records agreement. The Seller's Disclosure Letter also contradicts the labels, because it admits that Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay and the incident are unresolved. All 16 issues below are treated as open.

Figures are from the Seller's documents. Market ranges and rates are my commercial judgement and should be verified before we put them in the mark-up.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m).
- **Buyer wants:** A higher cap, with specific indemnities and fundamental warranties sitting outside it.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 30–40% (AUD 7.2–9.6m), with a fallback of about 25%. The cap is only tolerable if the known issues are carved out, since the identified items alone are about AUD 4.1m.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** A AUD 25k per-claim de minimis, plus a AUD 250k "excess-only" deductible basket (about 1% of price).
- **Buyer wants:** A lower de minimis, a tipping (first-dollar) basket, and aggregation of related claims.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at about AUD 10k de minimis and a AUD 120k tipping basket. A deductible basket plus a high de minimis strips out most realistic claims. Thresholds must not apply to fundamental, tax, fraud or specific-indemnity claims.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months, and any limitation "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise".
- **Buyer wants:** At least 24 months, so that two audit cycles are covered. Longer periods for tax and fundamental claims.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" language. As drafted it would sweep in title, tax, indemnities and fraud.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties are subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties capped at 100% of price (or the amount actually paid), with no thresholds. The time limit should be at least 6 years, consistent with the NSW contract limitation period.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Title is the core of a 100% share purchase, and a 20% cap and 18-month limit would leave most of the AUD 24m unprotected.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** No carve-out appears. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply to "all Claims of any nature", which on its face includes fraud.
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out removing all caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation and wilful concealment. It should extend to Seller and Seller-group conduct.
- **Recommendation:** Insert the carve-out. Excluding liability for fraud is commonly unenforceable or heavily contested, and the Seller's blanket wording invites argument.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Disclosure Letter 1.1, 1.2). Clause 1.4 adds that nothing is an admission of materiality or of any legal requirement.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific disclosure only, against identified warranties, with fair detail. The disclosed matters should not cut across specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general disclosure. It would neutralise most warranties, and it lets the Seller "disclose" the very problems it has not fixed.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Deletion. Failing that, limit it to the actual, current knowledge of named deal-team individuals of a specifically disclosed matter. It must not affect indemnities or price adjustments.
- **Recommendation:** Delete. Combined with general disclosure it removes almost all warranty protection, and "discoverable" imposes a constructive-knowledge standard.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** "Reasonable endeavours", with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (about 30%). The Disclosure Letter admits no final consent or evidence that the DD-002 clause 11.3 conditions are met.
- **Buyer wants:** A true condition precedent: written consent in form and substance satisfactory to the Buyer, with no adverse conditions, and the 11.3 conditions satisfied. It also wants a long-stop date, a Buyer-only waiver right, and a termination right.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the Seller's wording. Consider a price protection mechanism if the Buyer chooses to waive. Loss of 30% of revenue goes to the heart of the valuation.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** A release "to be provided following Completion". About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, and the Disclosure Letter confirms no repayment and no discharge.
- **Buyer wants:** Repayment at Completion out of the price, under a payout letter, with delivery at Completion of security releases and discharges (including PPSR). This is what "debt-free" means.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release. Deduct the payout amount from the price at Completion. Otherwise the Buyer inherits secured debt and a change-of-control default risk (DD-003 clause 8.1).

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** Treats the AUD 420,000 of DD-005 Completion bonuses as the Seller's matter, not itemised in the funds flow.
- **Buyer wants:** The bonuses treated as a Seller transaction cost or debt-like item and deducted from the price, or paid through the funds flow. On-costs should be added: superannuation (12% currently) and NSW payroll tax (verify the rate). The Disclosure Letter says it does not state whether these apply.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Bonuses triggered by the sale and payable by the Company should reduce the price, and an unitemised "Seller matter" does not bind the Company.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** The existing indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate".
- **Buyer wants:** An indemnity broad enough to cover IP ownership and title to the SOW3 Project Materials, plus claims, licence or infringement exposure and costs. DD-004 clause 7.3 makes transfer of materials conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180k open, which is not independent bank verification. There is no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- **Recommendation:** Reject as inadequate. Require pre-Completion payment evidence and a signed confirmatory assignment as a condition or deliverable. Add a broader specific indemnity outside the cap, backed by a retention.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material".
- **Buyer wants:** A specific indemnity, uncapped or separately and highly capped, with no thresholds. It should cover investigation, notification, regulatory, third-party claim and remediation costs. It also wants a retention or escrow, conduct and cooperation rights, and a Seller covenant to complete the investigation. The Disclosure Letter says about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) may be affected, and it does not establish access, scope, or whether notification is required.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "not material" characterisation. The unknowns cannot be priced, so allocate them to the Seller. Get the assessment completed quickly, given Privacy Act notifiable data breach timeframes.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** The three renewals (AUD 330k aggregate, 3 × AUD 110k) are ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:** Clarity on whether each renewal is committed, terminable, already accrued or prepaid. The Disclosure Letter says it does not state whether they are unavoidable or ordinary course.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the characterisation yet. Request the contract terms, then treat any committed or accrued amount as debt-like or a working capital adjustment. Add a specific warranty on the ordinary-course nature of these commitments.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** Pre-labels clauses [STANDARD] ("cleared by both sides") and tells us to focus only on [OPEN] items.
- **Buyer wants:** Its own assessment of every term, and no concession by label.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the framing and record in the cover reply that no term is agreed until the full SPA is settled. Several [STANDARD] items (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, incident, caps, disclosure) are our biggest issues.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012. The Disclosure Letter says this only identifies the Seller's source and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification. This means ASIC and PPSR searches, the constitution and share issue history, signed share transfers and certificates if any, and confirmation that no encumbrance or option exists (including any Riverlark security over the shares). The title warranty should be unqualified and treated as fundamental.
- **Recommendation:** Do not rely on the register alone. Complete our own searches and make clean title a Completion deliverable.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Considers tax and IP "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** A pre-Completion tax indemnity (or tax deed) and tax warranties with a longer limit (at least 5–6 years, consistent with ATO amendment periods). It also wants IP ownership and non-infringement warranties given at a fundamental or higher cap level, and clear treatment of the Ironquay materials.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Tax and IP are core to a data business, and the general 20% cap and 18-month limit are inadequate for them.

---

**Overall:** The known quantifiable items come to about AUD 4.13m: Riverlark 3.2m, bonuses 0.42m plus on-costs, Ironquay 0.18m and Sandbar 0.33m. That is about 17% of the price, before the Bluefen revenue risk and the incident exposure. The price should be adjusted for these items, and not left to warranty claims under the Seller's 20% cap and 25k/250k thresholds.

**Suggested next steps:**
1. Send a cover reply rejecting the [STANDARD]/[OPEN] framing.
2. Prepare the SPA mark-up on the points above.
3. Issue a supplementary DD request covering Bluefen, Sandbar, the incident, tax and title searches.

I can draft the cover reply or the mark-up language next if you want.
